'''S-equivalence''' is an [[equivalence relation]] on the families of [[Stable vector bundle|semistable]] [[vector bundle]]s on an [[algebraic curve]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kumar |first1=Shrawan |last2=Laumon |first2=Gérard |last3=Stuhler |first3=Ulrich |title=Vector Bundles on Curves - New Directions: Lectures given at the 3rd Session of the Centro Internazionale Matematico Estivo (C.I.M.E.), held in Cetraro (Cosenza), Italy, June 19-27, 1995 |date=14 November 2006 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-540-49701-1 |page=14 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Vector_Bundles_on_Curves_New_Directions/kGx7CwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22S-equivalence%22+semistable+vector+bundles+algebraic+curve&pg=PA14&printsec=frontcover |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Definition ==
Let ''X'' be a [[projective curve]] over an [[algebraically closed field]] ''k''. A vector bundle on ''X'' can be considered as a locally free [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]]. Every semistable locally free ''E'' on ''X'' admits a Jordan-Hölder [[filtration (mathematics)|filtration]] with stable [[subquotient]]s, i.e.
:<math> 0 = E_0 \subseteq E_1 \subseteq \ldots \subseteq E_n = E </math>
where <math>E_i</math> are locally free sheaves on ''X'' and <math>E_i/E_{i-1}</math> are stable. Although the Jordan-Hölder filtration is not unique, the subquotients are, which means that <math>gr E = \bigoplus_i E_i/E_{i-1}</math> is unique up to isomorphism.

Two semistable locally free sheaves ''E'' and ''F'' on ''X'' are ''S''-equivalent if ''gr E'' ≅ ''gr F''.
